newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened further against the dollar on Friday in a calm market amid dollar selling from exporters, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.50 against the dollar from 56.87 on Thursday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 88.56 from 89.04 on Thursday.
"The dollar took a nosedive, depreciating by 0.5 percent against the local unit as exporter sales to the market brought about panic selling of the greenback," a dealer said.
"The dollar unit lost 300 basis points to end the day at 56.40/60 from 56.70/90 at open," the dealer said.
"The market, which has been sitting short shillings was subjected to a wave of dollar selling as players scrambled for short dollar positions," she added.

A commercial banker said "Sentiment still favours a stronger shilling with a number of traders seeing 55 as a realistic short-term level. Being the end of the week, most people are not anxious to change their positions."
Dealers said overnight money market was tight with many banks seeking funds. Rates quoted were above 15 percent levels.
